title: Stamp 3: The Vel d'Hiv Round-up
welcome_lead: Stamp the tragic memory of Vichy's complicity in the Holocaust.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on the Vel d'Hiv round-up of July 1942 and Jewish deportations.
final_note: Memory stamp earned. France's role is acknowledged.

concepts.def: Round-up of 16-17 July 1942 in Paris, arresting over 13,000 Jews.
Indoor cycling stadium where thousands of Jews were held in appalling conditions.
Internment camp north of Paris, transit point for deportation to Auschwitz.
Vichy laws of October 1940 and June 1941 stripping Jews of civil rights.
President's speech acknowledging French state responsibility in the deportations.
French citizens recognised by Yad Vashem for hiding Jews during the Occupation.

walkthroughs.body_html: On 16-17 July 1942, French police arrested 13,152 Jews in Paris (including 4,115 children). Most were held at the Vel d'Hiv before being sent to Drancy, then Auschwitz. Almost none survived.

On 16 July 1995, Jacques Chirac became the first president to acknowledge that 'the criminal folly of the occupier was assisted by French people, by the French State'. This broke decades of official silence.
La Shoah = the Holocaust. La deportation = deportation. Le devoir de memoire = duty of remembrance. Les Justes parmi les Nations = Righteous Among the Nations.
